summary:
Kedah's own criminal law is set out in the Syariah Criminal Offences (Kedah Darul Aman) Enactment 2014 (En.18/2014). Sections 23 and 24 criminalise liwat and musahaqah, punishable by a fine of up to RM5,000, up to three years' imprisonment, up to six strokes of whipping, or any combination of those penalties. Section 26 criminalises a male posing as a woman in public, carrying a fine of up to RM1,000 or up to one year's imprisonment. Female cross-dressing is not an offence under the enactment, so the state's public-presentation offence falls asymmetrically on trans women and on anyone read as male presenting as a woman. Section 52 allows a woman convicted of musahaqah to be committed to an approved home for up to six months in addition to the sentence imposed.

Enforcement in Kedah has reached private gatherings. In October 2020 a private birthday party was raided and 30 trans women were singled out and arrested, while the event organiser was placed under investigation for "encouraging vice". A coalition of Malaysian human-rights groups publicly objected to the probe, describing a pattern in which organisers and allies of transgender people are pursued alongside those who attend.
tangentialFactors:
The Kedah organiser probe is the documented local instance of a wider enforcement approach in which liability is extended past attendees to the people who host or support transgender gatherings. For a visitor, that means the legal exposure attached to a private event in Kedah is not confined to the person whose presentation or conduct is at issue; whoever arranged the venue or the gathering can be investigated as well.

Section 26's wording covers only a male posing as a woman, and the enactment contains no definition of what that presentation consists of, so the boundary between compliant and offending appearance is drawn by enforcement officers in practice rather than fixed by the text.
localsOnly:
For residents convicted under the enactment, the penalty is not only custodial. A woman convicted of musahaqah may be committed to an approved home for up to six months under section 52, an institutional placement that follows the criminal sentence rather than replacing it.

Trans women living in Kedah carry section 26 exposure in ordinary public life, since the offence is triggered by public presentation rather than by any act. The October 2020 raid shows that a private residence or private celebration does not insulate residents from arrest, and that arrests at such events have been directed at trans women specifically.
outOfScopeNotes:
The outcome of the October 2020 investigation into the Kedah event organiser is not established in the available sources, and no record was found of charges being brought against the 30 women arrested at that event.

No Kedah-specific prosecution or conviction statistics for sections 23, 24, 26 or 52 of the enactment were identified. No Kedah-specific entry or visa rules exist to report; entry policy is set at the national level. No Kedah-specific figures on violence against transgender people appear in the source inventory.
